rows.why: Most of S1 is plain addition. The rows that settle an open question are "0s" → 0 and "1d0h0m0s0ms" → 86400000, which need zero counts to be valid. Item 8 accepts zero counts ("0ms" and "0d" give 0 with no error). The "2d" row also needs days, which item 5 supports.
Item 1 asks whether whitespace around the string is tolerated. Its pick uses strings.TrimSpace, so "  45m\n" becomes "45m" = 2700000.

S3 mixes several questions: empty input (item 3), a bare number (4), leading zeros (8), inner spaces (2) and unknown or uppercase units (5). Item 7 covers the most rows: "1.5h", "-3s", "+3s" and the full-width "３s". Its pick accepts only ASCII digits, so it rejects all four. Note the "05s" row: S3 expects it rejected, but item 8 accepts leading zeros ("01h" = 3600000), so the implementation fails that row.

No item asks whether a count may be bigger than the next unit up, such as 90m instead of 1h30m. Item 6 is about unit order and repeats, and item 8 is about leading zeros and zero counts. Neither is this behaviour.
Item 6 asks whether units must go largest to smallest and whether a unit may repeat. Its pick rejects both, which matches every row: 30m1h, 1h1h, 1s500ms2s and 5ms1s.
Item 9 sets the maximum at 2^53-1 ms = 9007199254740991, which is exactly what S6 expects to parse.
Item 9 returns 0 and an overflow error for anything above 2^53-1. It checks each count and the running total, so it catches both the total that is one too big and the 20-digit count.
Item 10 breaks the value greedily from days down to ms and leaves out zero parts. That gives 1m30s, 1h30m, 1d and 1d1h1m1s1ms. The 0 → "0ms" row is item 11, which also agrees.
Splitting 9007199254740991 greedily with zero parts left out gives 104249991d8h59m991ms. The seconds are 0, so they are dropped, as S9 expects.

Whether the round trip works depends on the output format from item 10. Greedy d/h/m/s/ms output with no zero parts is always in order, so the parser takes it back: 123456789 → 1d10h17m36s789ms → 123456789.
For values below 0 or above 2^53-1, item 12 returns "" and an error whose message contains "milliseconds". That covers -1, 2^53, MinInt64 and MaxInt64.
